reasoning: The package is a standard AUR binary package (-bin) that downloads prebuilt binaries from the official x.ai domain with pinned b2sum checksums. The PKGBUILD contains no executable code in global scope, no suspicious network operations, and no execution of fetched content. The package() function performs routine installation and generates shell completions by invoking the installed binary itself—a normal practice. All successfully audited files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, LICENSE, requirements.toml, .gitignore) contain no malicious patterns. The disagreement was caused entirely by tool errors (HTTP 400 and HTTP 429), not by security findings.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is due to tool failures, not security analysis: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) failed to audit LICENSE (HTTP 400), Report 3 (openrouter/free, advisory) failed to audit PKGBUILD (HTTP 429 rate limit). Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) completed successfully and found all files safe. Since Report 3 is marked advisory:true, it doesn't count as a vote. The only complete audit found no issues.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) failed to audit LICENSE file due to HTTP 400 error
Report 3 (openrouter/free) failed to audit PKGBUILD file due to HTTP 429 rate limit—this is the most critical file for security assessment
learnings: Tool errors (HTTP 400, 429) should be clearly distinguished from security findings in the final verdict—currently they cause 'inconclusive' which triggers unnecessary escalation
When a critical file like PKGBUILD fails to audit due to rate limiting, the system should retry or use a fallback model rather than marking the entire audit inconclusive

Advisory reports with tool errors should not trigger disagreement-based escalation; the system should recognize when inconclusive results are due to infrastructure failures rather than genuine uncertainty
